Scientific studies show why everyone should play video games

I'm a an avid Gamer (from NES to PS3 and I have a PC with a shitload of games from Steam) but I disagree with this article. I think gaming is a leisurely activity that provides limited benefits. The article states numerous benefits but what it fails to mention is that it is within the constraints of the games logic. I can solve puzzles in Prince of Persia sands of time, that means shit in a Calculus exam. I can have great reflexes and super fast timing in Street Fighter 4, but that means shit in a board room when I'm tryin to diplomatically counter someone's point. The skills gained in a video game is limited to the video game itself most of the time, sure there are exceptions (and those exceptions have limitations) but I'm talking about the norm. Online gaming has the potential to take those benefits stated in the article and apply them to everyday situations because you are dealing with the spontaneity of fellow humans. Maybe AI will get better, but until then you can't replace human interaction and real life to gain skills.
